unified-diff.description: A unified patch, either as one text value or as a file manifest whose patch fields Leaf delivers separately on demand.

instructions.producer:
Pipe the exact Git patch, with Git's default `a/` and `b/` prefixes, through this package's producer script into the source:

```bash
git diff <base>...<head> | leaf package run diff patch_manifest.py | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

The script preserves native Git evidence keyed by destination path. It leaves judgment to `lf-diff`: each file’s patch is delivered and checked before its row appears, and textual hunks render when their file opens. A file the widget cannot present shows its refusal and reports it to you as the page's error.

lf-diff.description: A unified patch with per-file navigation and commentable source lines.
lf-diff.x-instructions: Without `source`, write the exact Git patch in the `<pre>` at column 0, HTML-escaped (& before < and >), or entity text in the patch will change silently. Keep Git's file headers and metadata, and make each hunk's `@@` counts match its lines. Keep the leading space on context lines, and write a context line that is only a space as ` ` so HTML parsing keeps it. With `source`, bind a page-owned patch feed or files manifest and leave the `<pre>` empty. Add `collapsed` to start every file closed.
lf-diff.x-example:
diff --git a/feeders/mount.py b/feeders/mount.py
--- a/feeders/mount.py
+++ b/feeders/mount.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def bracket():
-    return "plastic"
+    return "steel"

lf-call-diff.description: A commentable call-tree diff, linked to the `lf-diff` that holds its patch.
lf-call-diff.x-instructions:
Set `diff` to the id of the `lf-diff` holding the exact patch. Store CallDiff's plain-text output, unedited, as the source's string value:

```bash
jq -Rs . calldiff.txt | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

Keep the unchanged items in the tree as landmarks. In a large repository, give each widget one file or entry point. Don't copy the output into markup, add attribute reads as calls, or draw separate before and after diagrams.
